checks: Removing the selected positive term leaves a nonzero negative exponential phase, so W is nonatomic. Its negative probability is positive by the unbounded negative coordinate independent of the others. The convolution with the one-sided exponential gives a continuous density and the exact value at zero.

Multiplying the convolution by exp(v/p) gives an increasing cumulative integral, proving the asserted monotonicity for all real v. Tonelli on w≤v<0 gives the endpoint transform and boundedness of (-w) exp(w/p) gives finiteness.

Eliminating the selected coordinate at V=0 produces the same factor 1/p and the forced positive-coordinate value -w/p. Thus the actual coarea first moment agrees with the endpoint transform divided by p. As an independent exact check, for (1,2,-3) and selected p=1, f(0)=3/20, B(1)=9/80 and the mean is 3/4 even though this endpoint lies outside the common tilt interval.

The reviewed statement also covers one positive phase, handles the chosen coefficient without requiring it to maximize, and proves global monotonicity of the weighted density.

readability: The selected p is local to this theorem, and need not be the endpoint p of the common tilt interval.
